decisions.statement: Which of a page's keys are relations is read from the index rather than from a list written here.
A name reaches the index and the pages the change itself has.
A page the change takes away stops being reachable.
A page the index says names a page being taken away is judged though the change names no such page.
A name naming no page type is refused rather than looked for under each target.
That refusal holds whether or not the name would have reached a page.
A name narrowing to more than one page is refused rather than taken as reached.
Mortality is judged on the page type the name reaches.
A name reaching no page is judged on the property's declared target.
A name an entry row states is resolved, and the refusal lands on the row's page.
A name nested in a record inside an entry row is not resolved.
An entry row is read through the change rather than off the working tree.
A change carrying an entry file judges the page that file sits beside.
A property declaring more than one target is judged on the page a name reaches.
A name nested one record deep is resolved.
The refusal names the record and the field.
A name reaches a page of a page type the change itself adds.
A relation property the change introduces is judged.
Which pages named a page being taken away is read from that page's own references as they were.
That reading is of the edges into that page rather than of every relation property in turn.

definition: the check refusing a name that reaches no page, and a non-mortal page that names a mortal one
